title: Share or keep?

slides.title: Who made it?
slides.text: A picture, a song or a game level belongs to the person who made it. Finding it online does not mean you may use it.
slides.alt: Two My Blocks named Zig sit in the tray, and the second carries a based-on Starter blocks stamp: a remix keeps its credit.

slides.title: Read the badge
slides.text: Public domain: anyone may use it. Creative commons with credit: use it and say who made it. All rights reserved: ask first.

slides.title: Write a credit line
slides.text: A credit says what it is and who made it. It costs nothing, and it is how makers get found.
steps: art: dragon drawing by my friend
level idea: remix of my cousin's level
slides.alt: A Would You Rather online dilemma: something you made, and the choice of whether to share it or keep it.

slides.title: Keep private things private
slides.text: Your games can be shared. Where you live, your school and your passphrase stay private.
slides.alt: The mailbox key builder: pick words for a passphrase, the key that locks your mailbox in Packet Post.

words.means: a yes from the maker to use their work
a badge that says how you may use the work

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Write the credit line for a game you might make: who made the art, and whose idea it was. Then name one thing you keep private online.

talk: Why share anything at all? What is worth the risk?
